To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the faint-end slopes of LFs at z ~ 1-4 are consistent with those in the local universe; (2) at z ~ 3 the LF is ~1.5 mag fainter than at z ~ 4; and (3) the LF of DRGs at z ~ 5 is ~1.2-1.3 mag brighter than at z ~ ~3.5.

the rest-frame optical LFs of galaxies at 3.5 < z < 2 are characterized by a bright characteristic magnitude and a steep faint-end slope; the contribution of DRGs (defined by their J - K colors) is 14%-33% in number and in luminosity; the stellar mass-to-light ratio is ~5 times higher for DRGs than for non-DRGs, and DRGs are responsible for 60%-80% in the stellar mass density at these redshift

the rest-frame optical LFs at z ~ 3 are characterized by a bright characteristic luminosity, a steep faint-end slope, and a low normalization, and that the global luminosity density at 2.0 ≤ z ≤ 2.5 is ~2 times lower in the R band than the local value, while at 2.5 ≤ z ≤ 4 it is comparable to the local value.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of the optical LFs and the stellar mass function of galaxies at 1.4 ≤ z ≤ 4.5, and the contribution of DRGs and non-red galaxies to these functions.
the properties of galaxies in the redshift range of 2 < z < 3.5.
the evolution of the luminosity function and the stellar mass function of galaxies at z > 1.5.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the rest-frame U - B color of the population is a better indicator of the galaxy's stellar mass than the J - K color, and that the rest-frame optical luminosities of galaxies at 0.4 ≤ z ≤ 2.5 are consistent with the local values.
at z ~ 3 the global stellar mass density is dominated by galaxies that are both massive and red.

the rest-frame R-band LF of galaxies at z ~ 3 is similar in shape to that of local galaxies, with a characteristic magnitude that is ~1.2-1.3 mag brighter and a luminosity density that is 2-3 times lower.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rest-frame optical LFs at z ≳ 2 are characterized by a bright characteristic luminosity and a steep faint-end slope, which is in contrast to the local LFs.
the rest-frame optical LFs of galaxies at 1.5 ≤ z ≤ 4.5 are characterized by a steep faint-end slope and a bright characteristic luminosity.
the global properties of DRGs are similar to those of the general galaxy population at 2 ≤z ≤ 3.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DRGs and nonDRGs are distinct populations with different star formation histories.
the global properties of galaxies at z ~ 3 are dominated by the properties of the reddest population.
the bright-end LF of galaxies at z ~ 1-4 is consistent with that at the present epoch, while the faint-end slope is steeper at higher redshifts.
